comment: Mentions an observation of the heliacal rising of Sirius during the 11th year of an unknown king, probably from the 17th Dynasty.
modernSource: Belmonte & Lull, Astronomy of Ancient Egypt: A Cultural Perspective [Page number unavailable]
textualContext: ...an observation at Jebel Tjauti, near Thebes, of the heliacal rising of Sirius on II Smw 20 of year 11 of an unknown king (17th Dynasty), c. 1592 BC...

comment: Record of the heliacal rising of Sirius (Peret Sopdet) corresponding to the 9th year of the reign of Amenhotep I.
modernSource: Belmonte & Lull, Astronomy of Ancient Egypt: A Cultural Perspective [Page number unavailable]
textualContext: ...the Ebers medical papyrus, which records a Sothic date on III Shemu 9 of year 9 of Amenhotep I (c. 1526 BC)...

comment: Records the heliacal rising of Sirius during an unspecified year of the reign of Thutmose III.
modernSource: Belmonte & Lull, Astronomy of Ancient Egypt: A Cultural Perspective [Page number unavailable]
originalSource: Block from the Temple of Khnum at Elephantine
textualContext: ...an Elephantine block (reign of Thutmose III) which dates the heliacal rising of Sirius to III Smw 28, corresponding to 1432 BC...

comment: Bilingual decree from the time of Ptolemy III attempting to permanently fix the heliacal rising of Sirius to the first day of the month of Payni.
modernSource: Belmonte & Lull, Astronomy of Ancient Egypt: A Cultural Perspective [Page number unavailable]
textualContext: ...The Canopus Decree, where there is an attempt to fix prt spdt [the going forth of Sopdet] in II Smw 1 (First of Payni), as occurred in 238/237 BC...

comment: Establishment of the Alexandrian Calendar: The date of the rising of Sirius is implicitly deduced by the establishment of this fixed calendar under Roman rule.
modernSource: Belmonte & Lull, Astronomy of Ancient Egypt: A Cultural Perspective [Page number unavailable]
originalSource: Records of the establishment of the Alexandrian Calendar
textualContext: ...the Alexandrian Calendar, established under Roman dominion, where the heliacal rising of Sirius was implicitly fixed on III Smw 25 in 25 BC...
